You are auditing this software repository to report its engineering status into a portfolio dashboard. Explore the codebase enough to form a grounded verdict: read the README, the package/manifest files, the entry points, the main source directories, config, tests (or note their absence), and CI config.

Then output ONLY a single JSON object — no prose before or after, and no markdown code fences — matching this schema exactly:

{
  "readiness_label": one of "prototype" | "in-development" | "beta-ready" | "ship-ready" | "needs-attention",
  "readiness_score": integer 0-100 (engineering maturity / ship-readiness of the CODE, not business traction),
  "summary": "2-4 sentences on how the app is shaping up; lead with what it is and its overall state",
  "stack": "detected languages / frameworks / runtime",
  "strengths": ["short, concrete strings that cite specifics"],
  "concerns": [
    {
      "severity": "critical" | "high" | "medium" | "low",
      "area": "security" | "correctness" | "tests" | "ci" | "incomplete" | "deps" | "perf" | "docs" | "ops" | "maintainability",
      "title": "one-line summary of the concern",
      "detail": "specifics; cite files/paths"
    }
  ],
  "recommended_next": ["short imperative strings, highest-ROI first"],
  "integrations": [
    { "name": "third-party API/service, e.g. Stripe", "category": "payments|auth|ai|analytics|storage|push|email|sms|maps|database|messaging|other" }
  ]
}

Order concerns most-severe first. Be specific and honest — cite files and paths. Do not invent problems to pad the list; an app in good shape should have few or no concerns. For "integrations", list every third-party API or external service the app actually connects to in the code (payment processors, auth providers, AI/LLM APIs, analytics, storage, push, email/SMS, maps, databases, messaging, etc.) — real integrations only, not ordinary dev dependencies. Never include secrets or token values in the output.
